current_row.boundary_rationale: “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying” (web:Jer.18.1) opens הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.18.1, byte tier) -- the hadavar-asher-hayah-el-Yirmeyahu shape that opens this frame. The command “Arise, and go down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.2), ק֥וּם וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֖מָּה אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת דְּבָרָֽי (oshb:Jer.18.2, byte tier), and the performance “Then I went down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.3), וָאֵרֵ֖ד בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.18.3, byte tier; the same verse carries a ketiv/qere note on its own 'behold' clause just after, consulted and not spliced through), lead into a second, internal word-event, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.18.5, byte tier), and Yahweh's interpretation, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” (web:Jer.18.6), הֲכַיּוֹצֵ֨ר הַזֶּ֜ה לֹא אוּכַ֨ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָכֶ֛ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier), the same verse closing on the plain article-bearing noun, בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier). The application to Judah by name, “Behold, I frame evil against you” (web:Jer.18.11), turns the same consonantal root into a verb rather than repeating the noun: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) is a bare participle, byte-distinct from the article-bearing noun that names the craftsman at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 (sweep: 5 verses on the article-bearing form); the shared object is the consonantal root itself, which recurs at the wider, article-free search across the book (sweep: 10 verses on the bare root). That shared root, not a repeated token, binds the application and the people's own refusal, “It is in vain” (web:Jer.18.12), נוֹאָ֑שׁ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier), to the observed sign. The join that follows changes neither the divine mouth nor, until mid-verse, the addressee: the instruction “Ask now among the nations” (web:Jer.18.13), שַֽׁאֲלוּ נָא֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), repeats the same second-person-plural imperative-plus-entreaty shape already commanding Judah two verses earlier, שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier); its own formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), is subordinated to the back-linking לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh frame -- the identical formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier), already stands inside the command to speak at 18:11, so the same mouth carries both sides of the join. Third-person description does not begin until mid-verse: “The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing” (web:Jer.18.13), שַֽׁעֲרֻרִת֙ עָשְׂתָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), and the material runs through the snow-of-Lebanon comparison and the forgotten-paths charge to the sentence “I will scatter them as with an east wind before the enemy” (web:Jer.18.17), כְּרֽוּחַ קָדִ֥ים אֲפִיצֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב (oshb:Jer.18.17, byte tier), the divine answer the 'therefore' of 18:13 supplies to that refusal, keeping command, performance, interpretation, application, and reply one enacted-sign row.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding Jer.18.13-Jer.18.17 as a separate indictment on its own messenger formula was considered: the formula there, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), is subordinated to the back-linking לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) and repeats the same mouth already speaking inside the application at 18:11, so it does not license a fresh row and the material was kept inside the potter unit as the divine answer to the refusal it names.
current_row.literature_type_guess: enacted sign at the potter's house, command through application

current_row.device_notes: Jer.17.27, just ahead of this row's opening, carries a petuchah (single-witness, tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets). Inside the row's own span, Jer.18.4 carries a further petuchah, Jer.18.6 carries a further setumah, Jer.18.8 carries a further setumah, Jer.18.10 carries a further setumah, and Jer.18.12 carries a further setumah (tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets, disclosed single-witness). Closing the row, Jer.18.17 carries a further setumah (single-witness texture, tier-3 weak under the Prophets' owner addendum). Two further ketiv/qere notes fall inside the span beyond the one already disclosed at 18:3: Jer.18.10 carries a further ketiv/qere note on its own 'what is evil' clause, and Jer.18.16 carries a further ketiv/qere note on its own 'a hissing' clause, both single-witness and consulted from the inventory rather than spliced through. The closed vocabulary carries no separate indictment category for the divine reply now folded into this span (18:13-18:17); symbolic_act_report is taken as the closest fit, since that material remains part of the enacted sign's own report rather than a fresh discourse. A devising-root wordplay brackets this seam: the singular noun מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) stands once at byte tier and, at the wider consonantal level, twice book-wide; the suffixed plural מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier) stands once at every tier on the near side of the seam; and on the far side, the cohortative וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה (oshb:Jer.18.18, byte tier) stands once at every tier while the plural noun מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ (oshb:Jer.18.18, byte tier) stands once at byte tier, twice at the wider pointed level, and nine times at the widest consonantal level, only two of those nine falling in the surrounding chapters. The recurrence is disclosed rather than argued as a boundary signal in either direction.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh command opens the row: “Go, and buy a potter’s earthen container, and take some of the elders of the people and of the elders of the priests” (web:Jer.19.1), spliced כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) — the messenger formula followed by an infinitive absolute and a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, not an imperative, opening on the prophet as addressee and distinct from the potter-house visit that precedes it and from the prophet’s own petition just before it, building a new commissioned sign on a jar rather than clay on a wheel. The command names the errand (buy the jar, go out to the valley of Ben-Hinnom, 19:1-2) and the oracle to proclaim there (19:3-9), then turns to the performance instruction, “Then you shall break the container in the sight of the men who go with you” (web:Jer.19.10), before its own interpretation, כָּ֣כָה אֶשְׁבֹּ֞ר אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְאֶת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁבֹּר֙ אֶת כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier) — “Even so I will break this people and this city as one breaks a potter’s vessel” (web:Jer.19.11) — closing on the Topheth-house judgment through 19:13. Command, performance instruction, and interpretation stay one unit because the same errand and the same named jar carry through from the buying to the breaking to the verdict on the houses of Jerusalem; the elders of the people and of the priests, וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier), are named as taken along on the errand in the rendering, with no verb in the Hebrew governing that clause, and the witnesses at the breaking are instead הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier), the men who go with the prophet.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through Jeremiah’s public proclamation in the temple court (19:14-15) was considered: that scene still reports the same errand’s outcome, but it relocates from the valley of Ben-Hinnom to the court of Yahweh’s house and turns from the elders taken along to “all the people” (web:Jer.19.14), a scene-and-addressee shift treated here as the stronger seam.
current_row.literature_type_guess: enacted sign-act narrative: a shattered potter’s jar in the Hinnom valley pronouncing an unmendable verdict on Jerusalem

current_row.device_notes: Jer.18.23, just before this row opens, carries a setumah; within the span a further petuchah marks Jer.19.5 and the row’s own close at Jer.19.13 carries a petuchah of its own (WLC, single-witness, tier-3 weak corroboration in the Prophets). A ketiv/qere note stands within the span at Jer.19.2, on the gate name, שַׁ֣עַר החרסות הַֽחַרְסִ֑ית (oshb:Jer.19.2, byte tier), the unpointed ketiv against the pointed qere (single-witness), symmetric with the mark disclosure above. Interior neum-YHWH formulas recur at Jer.19.6 and Jer.19.12 inside the oracle’s body (sweep: 2 verses in ch 19) rather than at the unit’s edge, so they read here as texture rather than a closing device. The potter lexeme also links the buying and the breaking, יוֹצֵ֣ר חָ֑רֶשׂ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) and כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier); a sweep of the bare consonantal form returns 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses: 10:16, 18:2, 18:3, 18:4, 18:6, 18:11, 19:1, 19:11, 33:2, 51:19), nothing falling between Jer.18.12 and Jer.18.23, so the recurrence is texture inside the span rather than a device crossing its own opening seam, and it does not counter the sign-object distinction between the jar and the clay on the wheel.
